title: Reverse Integer
prompt:
Reverse the digits of a signed 32-bit integer `x`. If the result overflows the int range, return `0`.

**Example**: `123` → `321`; `-123` → `-321`; `1534236469` → `0` (reversed exceeds Integer.MAX_VALUE).

Digit peeling plus a genuine overflow guard — the gotchas unit made real.
hints: Peel with `x % 10` and `x /= 10` — in Java this handles negatives symmetrically (remainders are negative), so no sign special-casing.
Build the reverse in a `long`; after the loop, range-check against Integer.MIN/MAX_VALUE before casting.
(The no-long variant checks `reversed > (Integer.MAX_VALUE - digit) / 10` before each multiply.)

solution.explanation: Java's negative remainders (`-123 % 10 == -3`) build a negative reverse naturally — no abs needed (which would itself overflow on MIN_VALUE!). The long accumulator can't overflow for any 32-bit input, making the final range check trustworthy.
